Sintoo @ Jitendra Dixit vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21
March, 2023
Author: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery

Bench: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 56061 of 2022
Applicant :- Sintoo @ Jitendra Dixit

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Satish Chandra Dwivedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rahul Kumar Sharma
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.

Heard Sri Satish Chandra Dwivedi, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Rahul Kumar Sharma,
learned counsel for informant and Sri Chandan Agrawal, learned A.G.A-I appearing on behalf of State.
2. Applicant- Sintoo @ Jitendra Dixit, has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 07.11.2022 in Case Crime No. 126 of 2022 under Sections 376, 506, 120B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station- Hathras Gate, District - Hathras.
3. Informant(mother of victim) lodged an F.I.R. on 06.05.2022 against applicant and his mother that they were tenant at her house.
Present applicant entices her minor daughter and committed offence of repeated rape.

He has threaten that a video of the act may be posted on various social Sintoo @ Jitendra Dixit vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34078325/
1 media platforms.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mother of applicant has approved the crime and after applicant vacated rented premises, victim narrated the occurrence and thereafter F.I.R. was lodged.
4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that there is no educational document that victim was a minor.
Radiological report opined the age of victim is about 18 years.
Learned counsel referred a birth certificate to submit that age of victim was 20 years.

5. Learned counsel further submits that according to allegations, he has repeatedly raped victim for more than three years, however, no complaint was made by victim or theirparents despite applicant and co-accused were their tenant.
The alleged video having recording of the act of rape was not recovered, the applicant is in jail since 06.05.2022 and according to instructions, statement of victim has not been recorded till date.

6. Learned A.G.A for State and learned counsel for informant submit that applicant has committed offence of repeated rape of minor girl for almost three years under threat of posting video containing the act of rape on various social media platforms.
The allegations remained consistent in statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
According to radiological report, age of victim is about 18 years.
Since the statement of victim has not been recorded till date, therefore in case of bail there is a possibility that applicant may influence the victim.
7. LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text: In the present case, victim(a minor girl) was repeatedly raped by the applicant.

The dispute in regard to age of victim can be considered at the time of trial as well as considering that initially first offence was committed three years ago, therefore, even on basis of birth certificate, victim was a minor girl three years ago.

She has made consistent statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
making specific allegation of repeated rape on applicant and there is a merit in argument of learned A.G.A. that applicant being prior acquainted to victim, therefore, in case of bail at this stage when statement of victim has not been recorded during trial, he may try to influence the victim, therefore,
no case of bail is made out.

9. Accordingly bail application is rejected, however, bail application is disposed of with direction that trial court shall record the statement of victim within a period of 12 weeks from today, if there is no legal impediment.
Subsequently, applicant will have liberty to file fresh bail application before learned trial court.
